messages:
Oncall Bot: ALERT: p95 latency > 2.5s on /v1/generate across hosted-region-us-east-1 (pager: oncall-sre) :rotating_light:
Marta: I’m on it. Seeing spike started ~10:02 UTC, from our synthetic agents and customer reports. Rolling 5m p50/p95: p50 ~ 240ms -> 520ms, p95 ~ 380ms -> 2.8s.
Oliver: Any recent infra changes? kernel packages, hosts, sched?
Marta: We rolled kernel 6.1.26 -> 6.1.28 on ~09:55 in that region as part of security patch batch. Patch rollout was partial to 20% at 09:56.
Priya: Noted. Which fleet subsets are hitting p95? Serving-host-tag: gen-large-prod and gen-shared-burst.
Jake: Adding traces. I can see span durations blown up at "kv-cache-lookup" and "dispatch-to-gpu" spans starting at 10:02.
Emily: I'm on logs — lining up host logs and kernel dmesg. Seeing increased page_faults and some excessive migrate_pages messages.
Ryan: Perf counters (via perf stat) on one victim host show huge context-switch and involuntary-sched counts. Might be runqueue thrashing.
Marta: Triage plan: 1) Stop new canary kernel rollouts (rollback or pause). 2) Divert traffic from gen-shared-burst to dedicated pools if capacity permits. 3) Collect full perf+trace bundles for 3 hosts.
Deploy Bot: Kernel rollout paused in us-east-1 (batch halted).
Priya: Can we do a quick rollback to 6.1.26 on one node to compare?
Oliver: We should avoid mass rollback until we have a confirmed repro. But pause is good. Jake — can you attach a flamegraph and top spans?
Jake: Pushed a short flamegraph link: https://internal-artifacts/redwood/flames/1987654321 — top is "copy_kv_cache()" (heavy syscalls), then userspace waiting on futex.
Marta: Customer impact: some API calls timing out for ~7% of requests (errors + 504s increased). CS notified.
Emily: dmesg excerpt (snippet):
```
[10:02:14] migrate_pages: BUG: excessive pages moved from 172.31.45.12
[10:02:14] CPU0: node_hotplug: unbalanced memory node
[10:02:16] kernel: task nginx: Out of memory? swapping?
```
Priya: That looks like page migration thrash introduced by the new kernel NUMA balancing change. I recall 6.1.28 backported a more aggressive page migration heuristic.
Marta: Hypothesis A: Kernel change increased page migration/NUMA balancing which causes user processes to block and inflate p95. Hypothesis B: Kernel scheduler change increased involuntary context-switches for our inference threads (higher preemption).
Oliver: What perf events did you capture?
Ryan: Run perf top for 30s on a hot host: many kernel functions in top (migrate_pages, try_to_migrate, do_madvise). Also high page-fault rates in user processes.
Jake: Trace spans show waiting in I/O and futexes; GPU dispatch waits longer because CPU threads are delayed marshalling requests.
Marta: Live mitigation options: A) Route traffic to dedicated pool (lower p95 but may cost us throughput). B) Add temporary autoscale to dedicated and redirect 30% traffic. C) Roll back kernel on a subset after snapshot. D) Reboot suspect hosts to clear migration thrash.
Priya: Prefer routing + node reboots. Reboots are less risky than kernel rollback during business hours.
Oliver: Agreed. Let's open route change: shift 40% of gen-shared-burst traffic to dedicated-us-east-1-pool-2 for next 30m. Priya, can you trigger?
Priya: Routing change issued:
```bash
redwood route update --service gen-shared-burst --split 60:40 --target-pool dedicated-us-east-1-pool-2 --reason "mitigate p95 spike due to kernel-induced thrash"
```
Marta: Monitoring now. p95 dropping to ~720ms after reroute. Errors down from 7% -> 2.1%.
Emily: Capturing full perf+vmstat top output to storage: s3://redwood-debug/1987654321/
Jake: Also uploaded strace of agent process (30s) and eBPF sched latency histo. Link: https://internal-artifacts/redwood/traces/1987654321/strace.tgz
Ryan: Suggested additional check: compare /proc/zoneinfo and numa stats before/after reboot.
Priya: Rebooting two suspect hosts (host-172-31-45-12, host-172-31-45-18) with drain. ETA ~6min.
Oncall Bot: Host drain in progress. Maintenance window noted.
Marta: After reboots, p95 back to ~300ms on those hosts. Overall region p95 310ms. Still slightly elevated vs baseline but acceptable.
Oliver: Good. Next steps: 1) Collect timeline with kernel changes + rollout batch + p95 timeline + traces. 2) Run controlled test: repro on staging by applying kernel 6.1.28 to a few staging nodes with heavy inference load. 3) Prepare RCA notes.
Jake: I'll script the staging stress test and capture perf traces. Command for repro test:
```bash
# on staging node
sysbench --test=threads --num-threads=32 run &
python stress_infer.py --model galactica-8b --qps 40 --duration 300 --capture-traces /tmp/trace.tgz
```
Priya: For immediate post-incident mitigation, keep routing split for 1h and pause kernel rollouts globally.
Deploy Bot: Global kernel rollout set to paused.
Marta: Communication: CS draft: "We observed elevated latency in us-east-1 due to a kernel scheduling/NUMA change introduced in a recent kernel update. We've paused the rollout and mitigated impact by routing traffic and rebooting affected hosts. We're running tests and will follow up with RCA." Anyone want to edit before I send?
Oliver: Add exact p95 numbers and impacted percentage and that no customer data was exposed.
Emily: Also note that we captured perf and kernel logs and will share in RCA.
Marta: Sending update to CS and status page now.
Priya: Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for the deeper RCA loop.
Jake: Action items recorded: [Jake] produce flamegraphs and span correlation; [Ryan] collect perf counters + /proc/zoneinfo; [Priya] coordinate staging repro & routing; [Marta] runbook update for kernel-rollouts.
Marta: Closing on-call handoff in 25m. If any regression reappears, page oncall-sre immediately. :thumbsup:
Oliver: Thanks team, good mitigation. We'll reconvene after the staging test and produce final RCA doc.
Oncall Bot: Incident thread marked monitored.
